info.description:
Merchant API — Queek.

## Errors

Every error answers `{"error": {"code", "message", "field"?, "errors"?, "doc_url", "request_id"}}`.
Switch on `error.code`, never on the message. Codes: `ai_unavailable_in_test_mode`, `api_key_expired`, `api_key_mode_mismatch`, `api_key_revoked`, `app_embed_not_ready`, `app_grant_insufficient`, `app_handoff_failed`, `app_installation_gone`, `app_installation_pending`, `app_ip_not_allowed`, `app_proxy_failed`, `app_proxy_gone`, `app_token_revoked`, `bad_request`, `channel_gateway_unreachable`, `client_key_required`, `conflict`, `custom_domain_provisioning_failed`, `custom_gateway_forbidden`, `custom_gateway_kyc_required`, `custom_gateway_not_configured`, `custom_gateway_not_verified`, `custom_gateway_plan_required`, `custom_gateway_store_ineligible`, `custom_gateway_verification_failed`, `forbidden`, `gone`, `idempotency_key_in_progress`, `idempotency_key_reuse`, `insufficient_scope`, `invalid_client`, `invalid_client_key`, `metafield_definition_missing`, `metafield_filter_unsupported_type`, `metafield_namespace_reserved`, `metafield_value_invalid`, `metaobject_definition_missing`, `metaobject_field_invalid`, `metaobject_reference_invalid`, `metaobject_type_reserved`, `method_not_allowed`, `not_found`, `origin_not_allowed`, `origin_required`, `payload_too_large`, `payment_amount_mismatch`, `plan_inactive`, `private_key_required`, `requires_slot`, `resync_cooldown`, `route_not_available`, `server_error`, `service_unavailable`, `subscription_feature_locked`, `too_many_requests`, `translation_digest_stale`, `translation_locale_is_primary`, `translation_max_published_locales`, `translation_unknown_key`, `translation_unknown_locale`, `unauthenticated`, `unknown_product_ref`, `unknown_service`, `unknown_variant_ref`, `unsupported_media_type`, `validation_failed`, `vendor_access_denied`, `vendor_mail_sender_forbidden`, `vendor_mail_sender_key_unavailable`, `vendor_mail_sender_not_configured`, `vendor_mail_sender_plan_required`, `vendor_mail_sender_verification_failed`.
Each error carries `doc_url` pointing at its own entry in the error reference, and `request_id` — always a
string — matching the `X-Request-Id` response header. Quote it in support.

## Legacy top-level keys

Additive only, never a second contract: on error bodies the runtime still emits the pre-contract
top-level keys shipped clients read. `error_code` and `message` ride top-level on helper-produced refusals
(the shared controller and ApiError error helpers, plus the client-auth handler branches);
`request_id` and `doc_url` ride top-level ONLY on non-reissued controller-helper bodies (storefront, client,
developer and dashboard surfaces) — the Merchant API reissues refusals, so there they live inside `error`.
They are documented separately under `QueekLegacyErrorKeys`, which no operation references. New integrations
switch on `error.*`.

## Request ids

Send `X-Request-Id` (8–128 chars matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) to correlate your trace with ours,
or read the one we generate — it is echoed on every response, error bodies included, and appears on every log line
of the request. `X-Queek-Api-Version` carries the API version (`v1`).

## Idempotency

Send `Idempotency-Key` on a write and a retry cannot execute twice. Same key + same body replays the stored
response verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` for 24h. Same key + a different body is
`409 idempotency_key_reuse`. A concurrent duplicate waits 15s for the first to finish, then replays;
past that it is `409 idempotency_key_in_progress`. Responses ≥ 400 are not stored, so a failure stays retryable.
The slot is vendor + caller + METHOD:path + key. The body is the fingerprint, not part of the slot. Operations that accept the header document it as a parameter.

## Rate limits

180 requests/min per API key + IP, or storefront origin + IP when no key is sent. On top of that, a private (`sk_live_`) key carries its
store's plan quota: `free` 60/min, `social_media` 120/min, `starter` 120/min, `growth` 240/min, `scale` 1200/min, `enterprise` 2400/min. sk_live_ private keys only. A pk_live_ public key is shared by every visitor of the store, so it gets no per-store bucket.
Exceeding either is `too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`.

## Webhooks

Subscribe an endpoint per store and Queek posts the signed event to it. Topics are listed under `webhooks`
in this document; the body is signed with the Standard Webhooks scheme — HMAC-SHA256 over the base64-decoded secret, value `v1,<base64>` —
over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`, tolerance 300s. A rotation keeps the previous secret valid for
24h and sends both signatures, space delimited. Delivery is 8 attempts on a published backoff;
an endpoint failing for 24h is disabled and the merchant notified. Every operation names the one scope it requires. A write scope also returns, in that write's own response, the record it wrote — listing or reading records needs the matching read scope. A key acts for its whole store, never only for the records one person created. Additive-only under v1: new operations, fields and enum values may be added, but existing operations, fields, values and auth behaviour never change incompatibly. A breaking change ships as v2 alongside v1, never in place.

## Money

Every amount is a major-unit decimal string (`"1500.00"`), never a JSON float, always beside its `currency` code (ISO-4217).

## Dates

Every `*_at` field is an ISO-8601 timestamp with numeric offset (`format: date-time`); the platform timezone is Africa/Lagos.

## Deletes and creates

DELETE answers `200` with the envelope (`{status, message, data}`), never `204`. Existing creates answer `200` and new creates answer `201` — both statuses are documented per operation and neither will change under you.

get.description:
Requires scope `merchant-options-read`.

Lists this store’s add-on groups with cursor pagination (`limit` + `starting_after`, `has_more`/`next_cursor`; at most 25 per page). Each group carries at most 20 items with `items_count`/`items_truncated` beside them — read the group itself for the full member list before patching it. Only the store’s own groups ever list: a shared group is attach-only by ref and never appears here.

get.description:
Requires scope `merchant-analytics-traffic-read`.

Reads up to 30 days of anonymous storefront traffic for this store: daily views and visits, bot request count, and measurement metadata. Visits are not unique visitors because shared mobile networks can group shoppers. Bot requests count requests and are not views. Figures can lag live traffic by up to about ten minutes (daily totals refresh every five minutes and responses are cached for up to five); only the installed app's own key with this grant can use this route.

AppRequirementStoreRequest.description:
The requirements sheet for the calling installation (PUT app/requirements):
the app replaces its own {product → required line-property prefix} map in
one call.

Full-body PUT — send the whole sheet every time, so a retry replays instead
of merging and removals are explicit. Products are addressed by p_id (never
UUID) and must belong to the calling installation's store. Each prefix must
live under the installation's own `app.{slug}.` namespace.

items.description:
`present` (not `required`): an emptied sheet is the explicit
full-removal signal, and an empty array is a valid sheet.

prefix.description:

must live under the calling installation's own app
namespace, so one installation can never declare for

that is the token the storefront can adopt.

rider_approved.description:

stamped rider_approved_at (see EnsureClientRider). The storefront
shows a "pending approval" state when is_rider && ! rider_approved.

CollectedDefinitionRequest.description:
Manage the calling installation's form types (GET + POST
collected-definitions, PATCH collected-definitions/{definition}).

One request shape serves all three verbs, with the same field-type,
reserved-name, display and budget rules the dashboard enforces — every
surface accepts the same definitions. Installation types carry the `app_`
prefix and declare it here. The data class is always `collected` and every
definition belongs to the calling installation; neither is sent in the body.

Definitions are addressed by `p_id` within the installation's store. Types
owned by another installation are refused with a 403.

has_pages.description:
Whether entries of this type get their own public page at
`/{type}/{handle}`. A type matching a reserved storefront route
(cart, checkout, search and similar) is refused with a 422.

CollectedRecordStatus.description: Triage state of a collected record in the merchant's inbox. Values are merchant-set only (status is the one mutable column); rows are never edited, only triaged and eventually purged or deleted.

CollectedRecordSubmitRequest.description:
Submit one record under one of the calling installation's collected types
(POST records).

Values are validated against the type's fields — the same field rules the
dashboard enforces — and the per-definition storage cap is checked before
anything is written. Every record is filed under the calling installation
with source `app`: the body carries no source, so a submission can never be
misfiled under another source. Calls are rate-limited per installation, and
a validation failure (422) never consumes budget.

Types owned by another installation are refused with a 403.

values.description: Record values keyed by field key. Each value’s shape follows the field type on the definition.

CollectedRecordSubmitRequest.title: Collected record submit input

ImportThirdPartyOrderRequest.description:
Import an order an outside sales channel already charged for. Generic app
source attribution comes from the authenticated installation.

The payload is the platform's receipt, recorded as charged. Item unit
prices, delivery fee, discount and total are amounts in naira with at most
2 decimals (6500 or "6500.00"), like every Merchant API amount, and they
must add up: the sum of unit_price × quantity, plus delivery_fee, minus
discount, equals total. Each item names its `product` (p_id, UUID or slug
of a product in this store)
and, for a variant, its `variant` (p_id or UUID of one of THAT product's
variants). The old single `ref` is refused: product and variant p_ids are
separate sequences, so one number could name two rows. A product from
another store fails the import with a named 422, never a cross-store sale.

The customer travels as name + phone only and becomes the order's
`shipping_address` recipient; no customer record is created.

channel.description: Optional for generic app installations, which derive source from the authenticated app and must omit this field. An installed Chowdeck or Glovo app must send its matching legacy slug. A generic app supplying this field, or a legacy app sending the other slug, receives 422. Human-key legacy imports still require this field and may send either slug.

publication.description:
Optional attribution to one of the calling installation's active
publications (p_id or key). Omitted means no attribution. A
caller without an installation may not send it (422).

ref.description:
The old single `ref` resolved variant-first, then product, across
two separate p_id sequences — one integer could name two rows.
Refused outright (never aliased): the caller must say which.

unit_price.description:
Naira, at most 2 decimals — the Merchant API's one money rule,
as for shipping-zone rates: a kobo figure is off by 100x and
runs past these caps instead of posing as naira.

ImportThirdPartyOrderRequest.title: Import third party order input

MerchantAddonGroupRequest.description:
The single add-on group rows (retrieve/create/update/delete). {group} is
this store's p_id or UUID, resolved in authorize() — after the scope gate,
before any rule — so a foreign, global or missing id is the standard 404
and never learns what the body would have failed. No route `where`: a
non-numeric ref resolves to nothing (never a Postgres cast 500).

max.description: Maximum choices a customer may pick; 0 is refused with a 422 (use at least 1).

items.description:
No min: an empty array echoes (never detaches); omission
detaches only the addressable members the entries name.

MerchantAddonGroupRequest.title: Addon group input

MerchantProductAddonAttachRequest.description:
Attach (POST) and detach (DELETE) add-on groups on one product. {product}
is this store's p_id, UUID or slug; the detach {group} must already hang on
the product — anything else is the standard 404. Attach refs resolve to
this store's groups or shared (global) ones; unresolvable refs and a
variant product fail the body with 422, never a 500.
MerchantProductAddonAttachRequest.title: Product addon attach input

MerchantShippingZoneRequest.description:
POST shipping-zones / PUT shipping-zones/{zone} on the merchant API.

Zone rules match the dashboard's, except the rates: this API speaks money as
decimal strings in the currency's major unit ("1500.00", or a number) — the
same shape a zone read returns, so a read round-trips into a write. Values
are stored in the currency's minor unit; the dashboard sends minor-unit
integers directly.
MerchantShippingZoneRequest.title: Shipping zone input

MerchantStorePostRequest.description:

MerchantUpdatePostRequest.description:

Absent stays untouched; explicit-null clears ONLY excerpt,

`slug` is normalised to a URL-safe slug only when it arrives as a string, and
the scoped unique ignores the resolved row.

MetafieldDefinitionRequest.description:
Create/update a metafield definition on the REST developer surface.

`namespace`, `key`, `owner_type` and `type` are immutable after creation: a
stored value denormalises all four, so changing one would silently orphan
every value already written against it. Only presentation (`name`,
`description`) and `validations` may change, and a tightened validation is
documented as applying to future writes only.

The same rules back every surface that writes definitions, so all of them
accept exactly the same legal definitions.
MetafieldDefinitionRequest.title: Metafield definition input

MetaobjectDataClass.description: What KIND of data a metaobject definition holds. `content` is merchant content (designers, size charts): entries may be storefront-visible and carry their own pages. `collected` is data gathered FROM people (form submissions, applications): entries are never storefront-readable and never revalidate the storefront. The booleans (`storefront_visible`, `has_pages`) stay the permanent source of truth — a collected definition is always stored with both off, however it is written.
MetaobjectDataClass.title: MetaobjectDataClass

MetaobjectDefinitionRequest.description:
Create/update a metaobject definition on the REST developer surface.

`type` is immutable after creation: entries carry it, and reference values
resolve through it, so changing one would silently orphan every entry and
link already written against it. The field SET may be replaced on update,
but removing a field (or retyping one) while entries still hold values for
it is a 422.

The same rules back every surface that writes definitions, so all of them
accept exactly the same legal types.

has_pages.description:
Whether entries of this type get their own public page at
`/{type}/{handle}`. A type matching a reserved storefront route
(cart, checkout, search and similar) is refused with a 422.

MetaobjectDefinitionRequest.title: Metaobject definition input

data_class.description:
The definition's data class (`content` or `collected`). Read-only
here: it is fixed at creation and cannot be changed through
this API.

records_count.description:
How many entries a collected definition holds (null for content
definitions). Rendered on dashboard reads only, so store-key
responses never carry it.

MetaobjectRequest.description:
Create/update a metaobject entry on the REST developer surface.

Shape is checked first (`type` exists, `handle` is slug-shaped, `status` is
known). Each field value is then validated against its definition — an
unknown key or a wrong-typed value fails with a `fields.{key}` error.
MetaobjectRequest.title: Metaobject input

Bearer keys are withheld here too (dashboard, shopper page,

Import recognition: the sales channel that imported the order

The receiver's own fields coming back to them: typed metafields the
merchant defined, and the opaque metadata an integrator wrote. This

Free-form integrator bookkeeping: opaque strings in, the same

taxonomy_node_id.description:
A node with no categories input resolves to the category write;

sku.description:
Product-level identity/pricing for products WITHOUT variants.
Prohibited the moment variants are in play — variants carry their own

video_poster_url.description:
Optional still image for the video — falls back to the product's own

gallery_media_ids.description: The product's other photos, after the main one, in order (media ids of the store's files)

options.description:
Product-level options derived from the ACTIVE variants (no

addons.description:
Priced choice-list add-ons hung on the product (variation rows,

webhook payloads stay bounded. Unloaded → [], never a query.

Product-level flag, inherited read-only: variants carry no
is_digital column, so a missing parent reads false, never throws.

Registers a publication (a sales channel) for the calling app. Only an app
connection can register one; the key is a slug unique to the app and may not
be digits only.

PUT translations/{type}/{id} — register a batch of translations against the
current source digests. The body shape is validated first (at most 100
items); then each item's locale, key and digest is checked against the live
source text. Failures answer per-item codes (translation_unknown_locale,
translation_unknown_key, translation_digest_stale) and nothing is written
unless every item passes.

SendAppAlertRequest.description:
Send an in-app notice to the installing merchant from the calling
installation (POST app/alerts). The installation comes from the calling key
— the body carries no target, so one installation can never alert on another
installation's behalf.

Titles and messages are bell content by design: plain text, length-capped
like the manifest listing fields, rendered escaped on every surface. The
optional dedupe_key lets the app collapse repeats of one problem (one
failing import batch, one expired credential) inside the TTL.
SendAppAlertRequest.title: Send app alert input

currency.description:
Vendor chain, never the silent platform default: loaded relation first,
then the cache-backed lookup (zero DB queries on a warm cache).

content.description:
Self-heal on serve: run stored blocks through the canonical
normalizer so a legacy/malformed section (e.g. a gallery with a
null slide) can never crash the storefront render. Same sanitizer
the write path uses, so serving == what a re-save would produce.
Pre-normalized above (attachContentMediaVariants also collects
media_index from this exact array) rather than re-normalized here,
so content[] and media_index can never disagree with each other.

VendorOrderExtensionRequest.description:
PATCH orders/{order} — the developer-extension fields of an order, and
nothing else.

An order's state is NOT editable here: status, cancellation, rider
assignment and shipment each have their own endpoint with their own side
effects (stock, settlement, notifications, webhooks). Any field outside the
allowed set is rejected by name with a 422 rather than ignored — an
integrator who tries to cancel an order by PATCHing `status` learns it from
the error, not from an order that shipped anyway.

`metafields` must reference an existing definition for orders and never use
an app-owned (`app.*`, `queek.*`) namespace on this endpoint. `metadata` is
free-form integrator bookkeeping — replaced wholesale (`null` clears it),
capped in size and count, with no namespace rule and no definitions.
`line_items` merges per-line properties by key: an app mirrors what it
booked or issued onto the line it belongs to. Property keys from an app
installation key must live under its own `app.{slug}.` namespace; any other
caller writes any checkout-shaped key EXCEPT the app-owned `app.*` /
`queek.*` ones, so no merchant can forge or clear an app's keys. Keys and
values obey the documented caps.

metadata.description:
Free-form integrator bookkeeping: opaque strings in, the same
strings out. Never interpreted, never rendered — so the only rules
it can carry are size and count.

line_items.description:
Per-line properties to merge: a string sets the key, null
deletes it, keys you leave out keep their value.

id.description: The line item `id` exactly as the order object's `line_items[].id` carries it.

properties.description:
Key → value map merged into the line's `properties`. Keys are
`namespace.key` (lowercase, at most 64 characters); a line holds

QueekLegacyErrorKeys.description: Additive legacy-compatibility top-level keys the runtime still emits on error bodies — never a replacement for `error.*`, which is the contract. `error_code` and `message` ride top-level on helper-produced refusals; `request_id` and `doc_url` ride top-level ONLY on non-reissued controller-helper bodies (storefront, client, developer and dashboard surfaces) — merchant routes reissue refusals, so there they live inside `error` and the `X-Request-Id` header. Handler-produced bodies keep their own top-level keys with `error` stapled beside them. Not referenced by any operation response: new integrations switch on `error.code`.

error_code.description: Top-level mirror of `error.code` on helper-produced refusals (shared controller error helpers, client-auth handler branches).

message.description: Top-level mirror of `error.message` on the same helper-produced refusals as `error_code`.

request_id.description: Top-level mirror of `error.request_id` ONLY on non-reissued controller-helper bodies. Always a string when present.

doc_url.description: Top-level mirror of `error.doc_url`, same per-producer scope as top-level `request_id`: non-reissued controller-helper bodies only.
